title: volumeSum and VolumeDissection
content: `volumeSum` computes ∑ c.side³ using Mathlib's BigOperators `∑ c ∈ cubes, c.side ^ 3`. `VolumeDissection` extends `CubeDissection` with the field `volume_constraint : volumeSum dissection.cubes = 1`, replacing the placeholder `covers_unit_cube : True` with the necessary geometric condition that cube volumes sum to 1.
mathContext: For axis-aligned cubes in ℝ³, a cube with side length $s$ has volume $s^3$. If finitely many cubes tile the unit cube $[0,1]^3$ with disjoint interiors, the volumes must sum to $\text{vol}([0,1]^3) = 1$. The constraint $\sum_{c} c.\text{side}^3 = 1$ is a necessary condition for any valid tiling — though not sufficient (e.g., one cube of side 1 trivially satisfies it without dissecting anything).

title: Basic Sum Lemmas: nonneg, singleton, insert
content: Three foundational sum lemmas. `volumeSum_nonneg` uses `Finset.sum_nonneg` with the per-term hypothesis `pow_nonneg (le_of_lt c.side_pos) 3`. `volumeSum_singleton` follows by `simp [volumeSum]`. `volumeSum_insert` requires the classical `DecidableEq Cube` instance (declared at line 52) so that `Finset.sum_insert` can pattern-match on membership.
mathContext: These are the `Finset` analogues of the inductive case in $\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i = a_1 + \sum_{i=2}^{n} a_i$. The non-negativity uses $s > 0 \Rightarrow s^3 > 0$; the insert lemma needs decidable equality because `insert c s` may already contain `c`, in which case the sum doesn't change.

title: Volume and Side Bounds from Constraint
content: `cube_volume_le_one` uses `Finset.single_le_sum`: since each term is nonneg and the total is 1, every individual term is ≤ 1. `cube_side_le_one` then derives `c.side ≤ 1` from `c.side³ ≤ 1` and `c.side > 0` using `nlinarith` with the hint `sq_nonneg (c.side - 1)`, which expands to `c.side² - 2·c.side + 1 ≥ 0` and enables cubic arithmetic.
mathContext: From $\sum s_i^3 = 1$ with each $s_i^3 \geq 0$, we get $s_k^3 \leq 1$ for each $k$. Since $s_k > 0$ (positivity axiom), $s_k^3 \leq 1$ implies $s_k \leq 1$. The algebraic step: if $s > 1$ then $(s-1)^2 \geq 0$ gives $s^2 \geq 2s - 1$, so $s^3 = s \cdot s^2 \geq s(2s-1) = 2s^2 - s > 2(1) - s > 1$ for $s > 1$.

title: Volume Sum is Positive on Nonempty Dissections
content: `volumeSum_pos` extracts a witness cube from `Finset.Nonempty`, applies `pow_pos c.side_pos 3` to get `0 < c.side³`, then uses `Finset.single_le_sum` to bound the sum below by this strictly-positive term. The conclusion `0 < volumeSum` follows by `linarith`.
mathContext: The strict inequality $0 < \sum s_i^3$ is essential because the volume_constraint says the sum equals $1$, so the dissection is automatically nonempty whenever it satisfies the constraint. This lemma is dual: it confirms that nonemptiness implies positive volume — necessary for the `cube_volume_lt_one_of_card_ge_two` argument later.

title: Strict Volume Bound for Multi-Cube Dissections
content: `cube_volume_lt_one_of_card_ge_two` strengthens the ≤ 1 bound to < 1 when the dissection has ≥ 2 cubes. The proof case-splits on `lt_or_eq_of_le`: if equal, then the single cube exhausts the volume, leaving 0 for any other cube — contradicting `pow_pos c'.side_pos 3 > 0`. Uses `Finset.one_lt_card` to extract a distinct second cube, then `Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg` to bound the pair-sum below the total.
mathContext: If $\sum_{i=1}^{n} s_i^3 = 1$ with $n \geq 2$ and some $s_k = 1$, then $\sum_{i \neq k} s_i^3 = 0$. But each $s_i^3 > 0$, so this forces $n = 1$ — contradiction. Geometrically: a dissection cannot contain a unit-side cube alongside any other cube, because the unit cube already fills $[0,1]^3$.

title: Collision Pairs and Volume: 2s³ ≤ 1
content: `volume_dissection_has_collision` is a one-line corollary of `every_dissection_has_collision` from OQ-01. `collision_volume_bound` then proves that for any collision pair (c₁, c₂) with c₁.side = c₂.side = s, we have 2s³ ≤ 1. The proof bounds the pair-sum `c₁.side³ + c₂.side³ = 2s³` above by the total `volumeSum = 1` via `Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg`. `collision_side_le_half_cbrt` immediately gives s³ ≤ 1/2 via `linarith`.
mathContext: If two distinct cubes with the same side length $s$ appear in a VolumeDissection, they each contribute $s^3$ to the sum $\sum c_i^3 = 1$. Since all other terms are nonneg, $2s^3 \leq 1$, i.e., $s \leq 2^{-1/3} \approx 0.7937$. This is a quantitative upper bound on how large any repeated-size cube can be in a volume-constrained dissection.

title: Minimum Cubes for Collision
content: `min_cubes_for_collision` shows any VolumeDissection containing a collision pair must have at least 2 cubes. The proof unpacks the collision pair (c₁, c₂) with `c₁ ≠ c₂`, builds the 2-element subset `{c₁, c₂}` via `Finset.card_insert_of_notMem`, and applies `Finset.card_le_card` to bound `2 ≤ d.cubes.card`.
mathContext: A trivial-looking but necessary cardinality lemma: pairs require at least 2 elements. Combined with `cube_volume_lt_one_of_card_ge_two`, this means: in any nonempty VolumeDissection, every cube has strict volume < 1 (because OQ-01 forces ≥ 2 cubes via the existence of a collision pair).

title: Volume Sum Decomposition Lemmas
content: `volumeSum_union` lifts `Finset.sum_union` to the volume-sum abstraction: when finsets `s, t` are disjoint, `volumeSum (s ∪ t) = volumeSum s + volumeSum t`. `volumeSum_eq` is a definitional rewriting (`rfl`) that exposes the underlying `Finset.sum` formulation — useful when downstream lemmas need the raw sum form.
mathContext: These lemmas form the algebraic backbone for any future inductive argument over cube subsets. For instance, splitting a dissection into 'large' and 'small' cubes (e.g., side > $2^{-1/3}$ vs. ≤) uses `volumeSum_union` after verifying disjointness via the partition.

title: Satisfiability via Trivial Witness
content: `volume_constraint_satisfiable` constructs an explicit `VolumeDissection` with one cube of side 1 at the origin. The witness cube `⟨0, 0, 0, 1, by norm_num⟩` is built directly; `all_contained` verifies $[0,1]^3 \subseteq [0,1]^3$ via `le_refl`/`norm_num`; `pairwise_disjoint` is vacuous on a singleton (the only pair `(c, c)` is excluded by `c₁ ≠ c₂`); and `covers_unit_cube` is trivial because the base structure uses `True`.
mathContext: The trivial witness — one unit cube — exists and shows the structure VolumeDissection is nonempty as a type. This is logically necessary: without a witness, every theorem about `vd : VolumeDissection` would be vacuous. Note this witness has `card = 1`, so it does NOT satisfy the more interesting `cube_volume_lt_one_of_card_ge_two` hypothesis — those theorems become non-vacuous only for genuine multi-cube tilings.
